newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares higher, volumes seen picking up.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares higher, volumes seen picking up.

text.p: Austrian shares inched higher after getting off to a slow start on Friday, in line with Europe's main markets, and traders voiced cautious optimism for next week when trading volumes were expected to pick up.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips rose 4.75 points or 0.42 percent to close at 1,139.62. Among its constituents, 11 shares rose, eight fell and two remained unchanged.
"The underlying mood is positive," said a trader, adding that the market was likely to remain volatile in the short term. "A lot will depend on what's happening on Wall Street," he said.
Market participants said the ATX was seen stuck inside a narrow range of between 1,110 and 1,140 points.

Selected buying interest, mostly from institutional customers, drove some of the main issues higher. Steel maker VA Stahl was pushed to a new all-time high, rising 13.60 schillings or 3.5 percent to 402 schillings.

Privatisation candidate Creditanstalt's preferred shares were up 11.50 schillings at 497.50 as the political controversy over the planned sale of the state's 70 percent voting stake in the bank dragged on.

Airport operator Flughafen Wien continued this week's slide, falling 2.04 percent or 11 schillings to 527. Declining issues were led by hosiery maker Wolford, falling 2.39 percent or 31 schillings to 1,268 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index rose 2.38 points or 0.56 percent to finish the week at 428.84 points.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for January delivery were up 5.3 points at 1,140.3.
